turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics

**Training data pattern:** The highest-efficiency configurations cluster around two winning "recipes":

1. **n‑i‑p, FA/Cs‑rich mixed‑halide (Br+I) perovskite + SnO₂ (or SnO₂/TiO₂) ETL + Spiro‑MeOTAD HTL + Au contact, deposited via a two‑step spin‑coating process.** SnO₂ has a conduction‑band offset with the perovskite that minimizes electron‑extraction barriers and reduces interfacial trap density better than TiO₂‑c alone; Spiro‑MeOTAD/Au gives a well‑matched, low-recombination hole contact; the double spin‑coating step typically indicates an antisolvent/second‑pass process that improves crystallinity and reduces pinholes — this is exactly the profile of the top two training entries (22.91%, 22.045%).

2. **p‑i‑n, Cs/FA/MA mixed perovskite + C60 or PCBM/C60/BCP ETL + PTAA (not PEDOT:PSS) HTL + Ag/Cu contact.** PTAA has a deeper HOMO than PEDOT:PSS, giving better hole selectivity and higher Voc; C60/BCP fullerene stacks passivate the ETL interface effectively. These give the 18–20.3% training entries.

Within these families, additional interfacial passivation layers (e.g., PFN‑Br, extra fullerene sub‑layers, MoOx buffers) tend to push efficiency higher by suppressing non‑radiative recombination at the contact interfaces.

**Applying this to the candidate pool:**

- **c062** (FAMAPbBrI, nip, ITO, SnO2‑np|PCBM‑60, Spiro‑MeOTAD, MoO3|Au, two‑step spin‑coating) is an almost exact structural twin of the #2 training champion (SnO2‑np/Spiro‑MeOTAD/Au, double spin‑coating, FAMAPbBrI) — very strong candidate.
- **c093** (CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, PCBM‑60|BCP, PTAA, Ag) matches the second-best pin recipe (PCBM/BCP + PTAA) closely.
- **c085** (CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, C60|BCP, PTAA|PFN‑Br, Cu) matches the PTAA/Cu pin recipe plus an added PFN‑Br passivation layer, which should further cut interfacial recombination.
- **c034** (CsFAMAPbI, nip, TiO2‑c|TiO2‑mp, Spiro‑MeOTAD, Au, double spin‑coating) matches the mesoporous‑TiO2/Spiro/Au/double‑coating pattern seen in many 18–20% training entries.
- **c008** (FAMAPbI, nip, SnO2‑c, Spiro‑MeOTAD, Au, double spin‑coating) reproduces the SnO2/Spiro/Au + double‑step deposition motif common to the top-performing n‑i‑p devices.

These five candidates most closely reconstruct the composition–ETL–HTL–contact–process combinations that produced the highest efficiencies in the training set, while weaker matches (PEDOT:PSS HTLs in pin devices, MoOx|Ag or bare metal contacts without buffer layers, single-step depositions, non-halide-mixed Pb-only or Sn-only absorbers) are expected to underperform.

Final: c062, c093, c085, c034, c008
